t: You're looking at the Royal Artillery Memorial on Hyde Park Corner, a First World War memorial unveiled in 1925. It commemorates the 49,076 soldiers of the Royal Artillery who were killed in that war. The sculptor was Charles Sargeant Jagger, who had served in the war himself and went on to make many works on the theme of war. The architectural work is by Lionel Pearson, and Thomas Arthur Darcy Braddell is also credited as a designer. The memorial was meant to show artillery visibly, which earlier architects had struggled to do, so the commission went to Jagger.
